_doc: Completed T-0486 ledger. Every frozen-manifest member received a dated repository/source review and targeted exact/variant-name sweep. Unlisted overrides use the documented no-corroboration default; pending is empty.
default_summary: No reliable record in the reviewed repository newspaper/reference corpus, Chicago directories, digitized local histories and targeted exact/variant-name web sweep could be tied to this postal person with sufficient date/place/occupation/kinship discriminators. This is a documented no-corroboration result, not evidence that the person did not exist.
search_scope: exact-name and justified spelling-variant web searches

ll_woodworth_james_h.summary: Papers of Abraham Lincoln independently states that James H. Woodworth moved to Chicago in 1833 and owned a dry-goods business there until 1840. That chronology directly spans the October 1834 postal return and July 1, 1835 scene date and safely corroborates the identity and occupation, while later offices are not back-projected.

ll_wm_teall.summary: History of Michigan City places William Teall in Michigan City in 1834, identifies him among residents signing license applications, and records his early warehouse/merchant activity. Exact name and Lake Michigan commercial context make him a useful candidate for the Chicago postal entry, but the source establishes Michigan City rather than Chicago residence.

candidates.basis: Exact name, documented 1834 Michigan City residence and merchant/warehouse activity on the Chicago-Detroit lake corridor.
conflicts: Contemporary local-history evidence places him in Michigan City; no direct source ties him to the Chicago waiting letter.

ll_young_gideon.summary: Kane County local history states that in January 1835 a marriage occurred at the home of Gideon Young, who then lived at Naperville. The exact name, date and nearby northeastern-Illinois geography make a strong regional candidate, but Naperville residence competes with a Chicago-household inference.

candidates.basis: Exact name and explicit Naperville residence in January 1835.
conflicts: Naperville geography; no direct bridge to the October 1834 Chicago postal item.

ll_works_charles.summary: Later Winnebago County/Rockford records identify a Charles Works in the early community, including church membership and later county office. The uncommon exact name makes a useful regional lead, but the surviving evidence is later than the 1834 postal return and supplies no direct Chicago bridge.

candidates.basis: Uncommon exact name in later northern-Illinois community records.
conflicts: Evidence is later and centered on Rockford/Winnebago County; no target-period Chicago identity bridge.
